title: Scale from one-task autonomy to unattended queue throughput
description: After one end-to-end success, teach Guildhall to continue through multiple tasks, skip blocked work cleanly, and stop only when the queue is exhausted or globally blocked.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Guildhall can continue through multiple unblocked tasks without manual restarts between each one
Blocked tasks are explicitly surfaced and skipped instead of stalling the whole queue on first contact

notes.content: Chunk 2 is now proven live on task-012. On the latest bounded replay, the worker advanced from generated Supabase types to the exact use-workspace.ts surface, then Guildhall wrote a fresh recovery checkpoint (step 3) and bumped task-012 updatedAt to 2026-05-07T22:45:07Z while keeping the task resumable in_progress. The next blocker is narrower: read-only checkpoint steps can still fall through into the generic research-budget refusal path instead of graduating into a durable handoff.

Fresh task-012 replay after the chunk-2 live proof made the next worker-handoff leak obvious. The resumed worker still opens with a reflexive read-file even when the checkpoint already says to write the self-critique and hand off to review. Guildhall now treats that as a handoff-shaped checkpoint lane and answers the first read-only drift with a strict one-tool nudge that demands an update-task self-critique note (or escalation) instead of leaving the worker on a generic checkpoint refusal.

Fresh task-012 replay on the latest build closed the worker-handoff visibility gap and moved the task back into real review. Worker-authored notes labeled Self-critique now surface in the live API/review packet, and the handoff loop no longer gets stuck satisfying a Set task status to review checkpoint with another write-checkpoint. The next blocker is now reviewer reclaim throughput: task-012 is visible as a reclaim candidate in review, but the reviewer lane is not yet being resumed cleanly from that paused state.

Reviewer fanout is now constrained to the task boundary instead of each persona's whole worldview. Persona prompts now require blocking findings to tie back to an unmet acceptance criterion, a changed file plus concrete introduced risk, or an explicit scope violation; broader architecture/perf/API advice must be emitted as non-blocking follow-up ideas. Aggregated revision packets now preserve those follow-up ideas in a separate section so workers can see them without mistaking them for required changes. Workers are also prompted to perform an explicit minimum-scope self-review before handoff: list changed files, say whether the diff is the smallest useful change, and name anything that should be reverted before review.

Thread review-feedback cards are compact again. Instead of expanding the full reviewer packet inline, the card now shows only the short revision summary, the review pass number, and an Open task action that routes to the drawer where the full packet already lives.
